name: cad_script_guide
title: How to write a custom feature
description: Everything needed to write a custom feature for a part studio: the guide (what a script is, how to think about one, the rules of its sandbox), the Feature API's type file (the only functions a script can call), and the examples that ship (lightening a plate with a truss, isogrid or hex pattern; a slot between two holes; a bracket; a vent pattern; engraved text). Read this once before writing a script.

name: cad_script_list
title: List a project's custom features
description: The custom features of a project (the scripts in its library, which every part studio of the project offers under Custom features, This project): each one's name, what it does, its parameters with their types, defaults and limits, and its version.

project.description: Project id or exact name, as listed by list_projects.

name: cad_script_read
title: Read a custom feature's script
description: The source of one of a project's custom features, with its parameters.

project.description: Project id or exact name, as listed by list_projects.

script.description: The custom feature's name or id, as listed by cad_script_list.

name: cad_script_validate
title: Check a custom feature's script
description: Read a script in the sandbox without building anything: whether it declares a feature, and its title and parameters, or what is wrong with it and on which line. Use it for a quick check of syntax and of the declaration; cad_script_run is what shows whether the feature works.

name: cad_script_run
title: Run a custom feature on a part studio
description: Try a custom feature on a part studio: it is built as the next feature, on a copy, and nothing changes. The answer is what happened: an error with the line it came from, or the warnings, what the script reported, the volume before and after (and the mass with a density), every body with its volume, whether the result is a sound solid, the console output, and a picture of the result. Give the script as source (text being worked on) or script (one of the project's, by name). Scripts run in a sandbox with half a minute of work; one that runs out fails with 'took too long'.

project.description: Project id or exact name, as listed by list_projects.

document.description: Which part studio: its path as listed by get_project. May be left out when the project has only one.

script.description: Instead of source: the name or id of one of the project's custom features.

params.description: Parameter values by key (numbers in mm or degrees, booleans, enum keys, text). A face or edge parameter takes { kind, body, name } with names from cad_get_bodies (names: true); left out, pick parameters are empty, as in a new feature, and the others take their defaults.

density.description: g/cm³, to report the mass before and after (aluminium 2.7, steel 7.85).

name: cad_script_write
title: Save a custom feature to a project
description: Save a script to the project's library, where everybody in the project finds it in the Custom features drop-down of every part studio. A script that does not read is refused. With script, the named custom feature is replaced (features already made from it keep the version they were made with, and their rows offer the update); otherwise a new one is added under name, or under the script's own title. With add_to, the feature is also added to that part studio, with params, when it builds a sound result there (undo_changes takes the feature back). Run the script with cad_script_run first and write it when the result is right.

project.description: Project id or exact name, as listed by list_projects.

name.description: The name in the project's library. Left out: the script's title (or, when replacing, the name it has).

script.description: The name or id of the custom feature to replace.

add_to.description: A part studio (its path as listed by get_project) to add the feature to as well.

params.description: With add_to: the feature's parameter values by key, as for cad_script_run.

view.description: With add_to: the view of the picture (iso).
